# Dividend reinvestment

The general investment account (GIA) at Vanguard, the overflow once the ISA is full. Unlike the ISA, this one holds **income units**, which was a mistake I made in 2022 and am now living with.

## What happens each quarter

Vanguard FTSE 100 Index (income units) pays out four times a year. Last payments:

- 31 Dec 2024: £96.40
- 30 Sep 2024: £131.12
- 28 Jun 2024: £188.75 (the big one, UK companies pay most in spring)

Automatic reinvestment is switched ON (Account > Income preferences > "Reinvest into the same fund"). Each payment buys more units at the price on the day it lands, minus no dealing charge. Before Nov 2023 it was paying to cash and the cash sat there earning nothing for 14 months, about £620 of it. Annoyed with myself.

## Tax, which is the real reason this note exists

Reinvested or not, it's still a dividend for tax. HMRC doesn't care that I never saw the money.

- Dividend allowance: £1,000 in 2023/24, £500 in 2024/25 onwards
- 2024/25 total dividends in the GIA: £512.33, so £12.33 is taxable at 8.75%. That's £1.08. Still has to go on the return, see [[Self assessment 2024]].
- Every reinvestment is a new purchase for the Section 104 pool. Each one raises the average base cost, which lowers the gain when I eventually sell. Keep the consolidated tax certificate (VG-CTC-2024-88417). [[Capital gains on shares]] has the pool workings.

## Accumulation vs income, once more

If I'd bought accumulation units here the dividend would be folded into the price and I'd get a "notional distribution" figure on the tax certificate instead of payments. Same tax, less admin, no extra pool entries. Next time I open anything outside a wrapper: accumulation. The ISA side is all accumulation already, see [[Index funds]].
